text.div:
SYNTHETIC RECORD, NOT A REAL MEDICAL RECORD

  • Urgent retina consultation within 48 hours for blurred vision with new floaters in a man with long-standing diabetes: dilated examination, OCT, and treatment of any proliferative retinopathy or macular edema; same-day attendance for a curtain over the vision or flashes
  • Glucose: continue metformin and basal insulin, titrated slowly by a written plan so that the A1c falls gradually; rescue glucagon; diabetes self-management education adapted for low vision (a talking glucose meter, an insulin pen with audible dose clicks, large-print plans)
  • Cardiovascular risk: atorvastatin increased to 80 mg, aspirin continued, baseline ECG; cardiology evaluation of exertional chest tightness with a pharmacologic stress test, since calf pain limits walking
  • Legs and feet: comprehensive foot examination today; ankle-brachial index; daily foot checks with a magnifying mirror and a bright lamp, protective shoes; podiatry
  • Kidneys: repeat urine albumin and kidney function after any change in kidney medicines; no NSAIDs
  • Grief and mood: acknowledge the loss, PHQ-9 now and at three months, and an offer of the health center's grief counselor, which he accepted; call or text 988 if thoughts of self-harm ever arise
  • Coronary disease, with cardiology: metoprolol succinate 25 mg daily and nitroglycerin as needed; continue high-intensity statin and aspirin; no revascularization now for a small area of ischemia with stable symptoms; review with cardiology in three months or sooner for worse or more frequent chest pain
  • Heel blister: daily dressing by the visiting nurse three times a week and by him on other days with a large-print guide; heel offloading shoe; podiatry within two days; review weekly; a vascular surgery opinion if it is not healing within four weeks or the ankle-brachial index is very low
  • On the retina specialist's advice: aflibercept injections in both eyes monthly for three doses, then treat-and-extend; panretinal photocoagulation to the right eye once the hemorrhage clears, and to the left if new vessels persist; vitrectomy if the hemorrhage does not clear within one to three months; low-vision evaluation; aspirin continued; glucose lowered gradually, and a GLP-1 receptor agonist only after the retina is stable, with retina review monthly
  • Lisinopril increased to 40 mg and empagliflozin 10 mg started, with written sick-day rules; potassium and creatinine in four weeks; urine albumin at three months
  • Peripheral artery disease: supervised exercise therapy three times a week for twelve weeks once the heel has healed; podiatry every two to three months; vascular review if walking does not improve or any wound fails to heal
  • Dulaglutide 0.75 mg weekly started with the retina specialist's agreement, rising only if the retina stays stable at monthly review; ezetimibe 10 mg added; lipids four to eight weeks after the change, booked before he leaves the clinic

resource.title: Jackie Robinson synthetic care plan
resource.description: Sight-, heart-, limb- and kidney-protecting care for a 52-year-old Black man with long-standing type 2 diabetes who comes in with blurred vision six weeks after the death of his son. The episode covers urgent retina care for proliferative diabetic retinopathy with macular edema and a vitreous hemorrhage (dilated examination, OCT, intravitreal anti-VEGF injections and panretinal photocoagulation, as the AAO Preferred Practice Pattern describes); lowering glucose steadily rather than quickly, with the early worsening of retinopathy after rapid A1c falls and after semaglutide explained and a GLP-1 receptor agonist started only after the retina is stable; an SGLT2 inhibitor for heart and kidney protection; a high-intensity statin with ezetimibe; blood pressure and kidney care; coronary disease found through exertional chest tightness; the ankle-brachial index, foot examination and wound care for a neuropathic heel blister; low-vision services and diabetes tools he can use with poor sight; depression screening and grief support; and the equity of care for a Black man with diabetes complications, under the ADA Standards of Care 1971, the AAO Diabetic Retinopathy Preferred Practice Pattern 1970, the 1969 ACC/AHA PAD and 1968 chronic coronary disease guidelines, and the CMID monographs.

Glucose: continue metformin and basal insulin, titrated slowly by a written plan so that the A1c falls gradually; rescue glucagon; diabetes self-management education adapted for low vision (a talking glucose meter, an insulin pen with audible dose clicks, large-print plans)

Cardiovascular risk: atorvastatin increased to 80 mg, aspirin continued, baseline ECG; cardiology evaluation of exertional chest tightness with a pharmacologic stress test, since calf pain limits walking

detail.description: Guideline reference: GL-ADA-CVD-2026, GL-AHA-CCD-2023, GL-AHA-STROKE-2021, GL-CMID-2026

code.text: Legs and feet: comprehensive foot examination today; ankle-brachial index; daily foot checks with a magnifying mirror and a bright lamp, protective shoes; podiatry
Kidneys: repeat urine albumin and kidney function after any change in kidney medicines; no NSAIDs
Grief and mood: acknowledge the loss, PHQ-9 now and at three months, and an offer of the health center's grief counselor, which he accepted; call or text 988 if thoughts of self-harm ever arise

Coronary disease, with cardiology: metoprolol succinate 25 mg daily and nitroglycerin as needed; continue high-intensity statin and aspirin; no revascularization now for a small area of ischemia with stable symptoms; review with cardiology in three months or sooner for worse or more frequent chest pain

Heel blister: daily dressing by the visiting nurse three times a week and by him on other days with a large-print guide; heel offloading shoe; podiatry within two days; review weekly; a vascular surgery opinion if it is not healing within four weeks or the ankle-brachial index is very low

On the retina specialist's advice: aflibercept injections in both eyes monthly for three doses, then treat-and-extend; panretinal photocoagulation to the right eye once the hemorrhage clears, and to the left if new vessels persist; vitrectomy if the hemorrhage does not clear within one to three months; low-vision evaluation; aspirin continued; glucose lowered gradually, and a GLP-1 receptor agonist only after the retina is stable, with retina review monthly
Lisinopril increased to 40 mg and empagliflozin 10 mg started, with written sick-day rules; potassium and creatinine in four weeks; urine albumin at three months

detail.description: Guideline reference: GL-ADA-CKD-2026, GL-ADA-CVD-2026, GL-KDIGO-CKD-2024, GL-CMID-2026

code.text: Peripheral artery disease: supervised exercise therapy three times a week for twelve weeks once the heel has healed; podiatry every two to three months; vascular review if walking does not improve or any wound fails to heal

Dulaglutide 0.75 mg weekly started with the retina specialist's agreement, rising only if the retina stays stable at monthly review; ezetimibe 10 mg added; lipids four to eight weeks after the change, booked before he leaves the clinic

code.text: Referral to ophthalmology (retina)

note.text: Urgent retina consultation within 48 hours for blurred vision with new floaters in a man with long-standing diabetes: dilated examination, OCT, and treatment of any proliferative retinopathy or macular edema; same-day attendance for a curtain over the vision or flashes
